name: TiMem

paper.title: TiMem: Temporal-Hierarchical Memory Consolidation for Long-Horizon Conversational Agents

construction.unit: node of a five-level Temporal Memory Tree: L1 fragment, L2 session, L3 day, L4 week, L5 monthly profile
construction.kept_as: L1: third-person LLM rewrite of one exchange (new facts only); L2-L5: LLM summaries, pattern reports and profiles
construction.processing: L1 written after every user-assistant exchange; each higher node is written by an LLM from its children in a closed time window plus the last 3 memories at its own level, with a level-specific prompt

organization.structure: temporal tree with explicit parent-child links; each node covers a time interval inside its parent's
organization.stores: PostgreSQL tables per level + parent-child relation table; Qdrant vectors
organization.index: Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B dense over content; BM25 over title + content, computed at query time

management.operations: scheduled consolidation: session, day, week and month nodes written when their window closes; the profile is refined from the previous profiles
management.conflicts: none at storage; the recall gate is said to drop redundant or conflicting memories at read time

retrieval.query: question for dense search; an LLM planner labels complexity (simple / hybrid / complex) and extracts 1-3 keywords (no names) for BM25
retrieval.candidates: L1 only: dense top 40 + BM25 over all L1 of the conversation, fused 0.9 / 0.1, top 20; then ancestors of those leaves at the levels the complexity label opens
retrieval.selection: one LLM gate call keeps or drops each candidate
retrieval.budget: 20 L1 + up to L2 4, L3 2, L4 2, L5 1 (code, LoCoMo); ~511 tokens after gating on LoCoMo, ~1,271 on LongMemEval-S

use.context: kept memories grouped by level (L1 to L5), each prefixed with its date; Mem0 QA prompt on LoCoMo, LongMemEval non-CoT prompt

classify.note: Hybrid dense + BM25 picks the L1 leaves; higher levels arrive by fixed parent links; an LLM gate makes the final keep/drop call, so 'LLM decides' rather than 'top-k rule'.

stages.ingestion: The dialogue is cut into fixed windows of one user-assistant exchange (w_d = 1); no semantic segmentation.
stages.construction: An LLM rewrites each exchange into a third-person L1 fragment that keeps only facts not already in the last 3 fragments; relative times are left as written.
stages.organization: Fragments are the leaves of a Temporal Memory Tree: L2 session, L3 day, L4 week and L5 monthly profile nodes, each with a time interval that contains its children's, linked parent to child.
stages.update: When a session, day, week or month closes, an LLM writes the parent node from its children plus the last 3 nodes at that level, with a level-specific prompt (facts, events, patterns, profile). Nothing is deleted or edited afterwards.
stages.retrieval: An LLM planner labels the question simple, hybrid or complex and extracts keywords; dense + BM25 over L1 picks 20 leaves; their ancestors at the levels opened by the label are added through parent links; an LLM gate keeps or drops each candidate.
stages.answer: The answer model reads the kept memories grouped by level, each with its date, under level headers.

summary: Dialogue is rewritten exchange by exchange into leaf memories and consolidated on a calendar schedule into session, day, week and monthly-profile nodes of a temporal tree; recall searches only the leaves, climbs parent links to levels chosen by a query-complexity planner, and filters with an LLM gate.
notes: VENUE: Findings of ACL 2026, verified in the ACL Anthology (2026.findings-acl.1091, https://aclanthology.org/2026.findings-acl.1091/); the arXiv comment also says ACL 2026 Findings. Text read from arXiv v2 (30 Apr 2026). Code: github.com/TiMEM-AI/timem pinned at 6d279a5 (HEAD, 2026-05-27); retrieval, config and experiment code are identical to the initial commit f369184 (2026-02-08) except one import line. TAXONOMY CHECK (not edited here): consolidation-trigger 'scheduled-periodic' is right for L2-L5 (written when a session/day/week/month window closes, §3.2.2, App. B.1; code 01_memory_generation.py simulates a 02:00 daily backfill). retrieval-traversal 'top-down-routing' is wrong: recall is bottom-up (search L1 leaves by dense + BM25, then follow parent links upward; the code class is BottomUpRetrieverBase), which fits 'similarity-plus-aggregation'. DESIGN: trigger=every-exchange is the L1 write; higher levels are scheduled, hence management.timing=both. control.management=fixed-rule because the calendar decides when to consolidate (the writing itself is a prompted LLM). Baselines: the paper says it ran all five with their recommended configurations under one LLM/embedding setup (§4.1, App. B.2), so run_by=rerun.

sources.code_note: Official repository linked from the paper. It has 7 commits; the first (f369184, 2026-02-08) is after paper v1 and already contains the retrieval, config and experiment scripts. Later commits change README, licence, CLI and restore two model/schema modules; retrieval code differs by one import line. Pinned at HEAD 6d279a5 (2026-05-27). Whether this is exactly the code behind the v2 tables is not stated.

headline: Only L1 fragments are searched. Session, day, week and profile memories reach the answer only as ancestors of the 20 best-matching fragments, found by parent links, never by their own similarity to the question.
An LLM gate then cuts the candidates from about 4.4k to 0.5k tokens on LoCoMo (Table 3), and the answer model reads what survives, grouped by level.
In the released code the complexity-specific gate prompts are not wired in: the dataset config names templates the prompt file does not contain, so a generic keep/drop prompt runs.

open_questions: Table 4's 'L1 only, hierarchical recall' (73.18 / 72.40) beats flat recall over the full tree; with no higher levels it is unclear what the hierarchical path adds beyond the gate and fewer tokens, and the paper does not define flat recall precisely.

No run gives the higher levels their own similarity search, so the tests cannot tell whether session/day/week summaries help because of their content or because they widen context around the chosen leaves.
On LoCoMo L2 and L3 counts are equal (272 each): with one session per day, the day level mostly restates the session level.

glance.a: A node of a time tree: an L1 fragment is an LLM rewrite of one exchange; above it sit session, day, week and monthly-profile nodes, each written by an LLM from its children.
Each exchange is rewritten in third person keeping only new facts; the higher levels are summaries of 200-600 words. The raw turns are stored but never read.
glance.src: paper App. E.3; code postgres_store.py L134-L156

glance.a: By the calendar, not by topic: a parent node covers the time window of its children (session, day, week, month), linked explicitly parent to child.
No cross-encoder. One LLM call reads all candidates and returns the ids to keep.

glance.q: Is memory reconstructed at question time?
glance.a: No second search. The planner only chooses which levels to collect; an answer-time reflection loop exists in the code but the evaluation prompts never trigger it.

glance.q: What does the answer model read?
glance.a: Up to 20 fragments plus a few session/day/week summaries and the profile, whatever the gate kept, each with a date: about 511 tokens on LoCoMo.

steps.what: L1 fragments scored (dense top 40, BM25 over all)
kept by the LLM gate (LoCoMo average)

funnel.src: code bottom_up_retriever_base.py L125-L531, retrieval_config.yaml L56-L110; paper Table 6

flow.title: Label the question
flow.sees: The question only. Questions about preferences, prediction or reasoning go to complex; multi-fact questions to hybrid; single facts to simple. Personal names are banned from the keywords.
flow.src: paper App. E.3.7; code llm_retrieval_planner.py L185-L255

flow.title: Search the fragments
flow.out: every L1 with a fused score
flow.sees: Dense: the question against each fragment's content, top 40. BM25: the keywords against title + content of every fragment of the conversation pair. Scores are divided by their maximum and summed 0.9 / 0.1; fragments outside the dense top 40 get only the BM25 part.

flow.title: Keep 20 leaves
flow.method: rule: top 20 by fused score, then sorted by time
flow.sees: Scores only. The 20 are then put in time order, which also sets the order of the next step.

flow.title: Collect ancestors
flow.method: rule: follow parent links from each leaf
flow.sees: No text is compared. For each leaf (oldest first) the code walks L2→L3→L4→L5 and keeps a parent at each level the label opened until that level's quota is full; a session is taken once.

flow.title: Gate
flow.method: LLM judgement over the whole list, temperature 0.3
flow.sees: Each candidate as "[n-level] title", its content, time and session id, with the question. If it keeps nothing, the first 5 are used.

flow.title: Answer
flow.sees: Kept memories grouped by level with headers, each as "[date] content", oldest first within a level. No original turns.

An LLM gate keeps the useful ones; the answer model reads them grouped by level.

discussion.takeaway: Organise conversational memory by the calendar (exchange, session, day, week, month) and let an LLM consolidate each closed window; at question time search only the finest level, pull in the ancestors, and let an LLM prune. In its own tests this is the best of six systems on LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S with the shortest context on LoCoMo.

claims.claim: State-of-the-art accuracy among evaluated memory systems.
claims.evidence: LoCoMo LLJ 75.30 vs MemOS 69.24; LongMemEval-S 76.88 vs MemOS 68.68 (gpt-4o-mini), 78.96 vs 73.07 (gpt-4o). Tables 1-2
511 tokens per LoCoMo question, 52.2% below Mem0's 1,070. Table 6, §4.5

claims.claim: The planner and the gate both help.
claims.evidence: No gate 72.99 / 73.80; best fixed scope with gate 73.38 / 75.00; full 75.30 / 76.88. Table 3

claims.claim: The full hierarchy beats either part alone.
Consolidation separates users on LoCoMo and reduces spread on LongMemEval-S.
claims.evidence: Silhouette 0.093 → 0.574 from L1 to L5; spread 0.692 → 0.345. Fig. 3, Tables 11-12

limits: Consolidation and recall rely on general-purpose LLMs through prompts; smaller fine-tuned models might be cheaper.
Higher levels are free text without categories or knowledge graphs.
Time boundaries are fixed (session, day, week, month) rather than detected.
reading: Higher levels are never searched by the question; they only arrive as parents of the 20 leaves, so the tree adds context around what dense + BM25 already found rather than finding new evidence.
In the code the leaves are put in time order before the parent walk, so the level quotas (e.g. 4 sessions) are filled from the earliest matching leaves, not the most relevant ones.
The released config does not load the complexity-specific gate prompts shown in App. E.3.6; if the reported runs used this config, the gate was a generic keep/drop prompt.
Complex-query budgets in Table 7 (L2 8, L3 4) are twice the LoCoMo config values (L2 4, L3 2).

Baselines were rerun by the authors with gpt-4o-mini, Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B and k = 20 for all; each baseline's own retrieval settings may differ from its paper, and the number of runs behind the ± values is not stated.
LoCoMo numbers use Mem0's lenient judge prompt over 1,540 questions (adversarial excluded), so they are comparable only with rows using the same judge.

abstract.text: TiMem stores a long conversation as a time-ordered tree: each exchange becomes a short LLM-written fragment, and fragments are consolidated on a schedule into session, day, week and monthly-profile memories, each covering the time span of its children. No model is fine-tuned; each level has its own prompt. At question time an LLM judges how complex the question is, fragments are found by dense and keyword search, their ancestors at the matching levels are added, and an LLM gate keeps only what is needed. The authors report the best accuracy among evaluated systems on LoCoMo (75.30) and LongMemEval-S (76.88) with about half Mem0's recalled context on LoCoMo.
